seg_object_counts_match — SEGMENTATION score op

• Data kinds: labels2d × labels2d → table

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.seg_object_counts_match(labels_pred, labels_true, *, background: 'int' = 0, min_overlap: 'float' = 0.5) -> 'Dict[str, object]' (to call the implementation directly, import segeval; segeval.seg_object_counts_match(labels_pred, labels_true, *, background: 'int' = 0, min_overlap: 'float' = 0.5) -> 'Dict[str, object]'; from the registry, opssegmentation.get("seg_object_counts_match"))

Usage

Object-count agreement: counts split / merged / missed / false / matched from the degrees of a 'mainly overlapping' bipartite graph (seg_object_counts_match).

Condition for placing an edge between true i and prediction j (both non-background) = overlap n_ij ≥ min_overlap × min(|i|, |j|) (the smaller one lies mainly inside the other). With true degree d_i and predicted degree e_j:

missed = #{d_i = 0}, false = #{e_j = 0}, split = #{d_i ≥ 2} (1 true object split into several predictions), merged = #{e_j ≥ 2} (1 prediction swallowed several true objects), matched = #{d_i = 1 and its partner has e_j = 1}. counts_match = the numbers of true and predicted objects are equal and all match. With min_overlap > 0.5 each prediction "lies mainly inside" at most 1 true object, but there are also edges with a small true object and a large prediction, so merges can still be detected.

Returns: the counts above + n_true / n_pred, edges (true label, predicted label) as (m, 2), split_true / merged_pred / missed_true / false_pred (label arrays), min_overlap.
